question: The marked price of a study table is ₹3,200. It will be offered for ₹2,448 after two successive discounts. If the first discount is 10%, the second discount is:
solution:
Given:

Marked price = Rs. 3200

First Discount % = 10%

S.P = Rs. 2,448

Formula used:

Total discount% = - X - Y + (XY/100)

Calculation:

Let the second discount be x%.

∵ Discount % = - 10 - x + (10x)/(100)= (100+9x)/(10)

Now, S.P = (100-D\%)/(100)× M.P

⇒ 2448 = (100 -frac{(100+9x))/(10)}{100}× 3200

⇒ 2448 = (900-9x)/(1000)× 3200

⇒ (2448)/(16)×5 = 900 - 9x

⇒ 765 = 900 - 9x

⇒ 9x = 135

⇒ x = 15

∴ The second discount on the item is 15%.

First discount 10%, after the first discount Selling price

⇒ 3200 × (100 - 10)/100

⇒ 2880

Final Selling price = 2448

Second discount % = (2880 - 2448)/2880 × 100

⇒ 432/2880 × 100

⇒ 15%

∴ The second discount on the item is 15%.
